chapter: Japan trip, publishing and early influences
title: How the Japan trip came about: the Fuji Bank secretary and Koyama
summary: Late one night Japanese visitors came to his apartment and invited him to do concerts and albums in Japan.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Under what circumstances did you go to Japan?
And when I looked at this picture real close, up in the corner there is Ornette Coleman. See him there? Did you see him there way up in the shadows, can you see him there?
I don't see where. Yes, here he is.
I wouldn't have recognised him from those.
Well what happened was, about twelve o'clock one night and there's a knock on the door and these men, these Japanese men were there. They came in.
You mean here at your apartment?

Yes. And the man whose named (Shigawa? was the Secretary of the, to the President of the Fuji Bank of Japan? . He travels all over the world (and can prizes any where and there's big money in that?) He's there. So, he happened to be going through town and apparently the president doesn't let him off until late so (Unintelligible ?) it's always at midnight you know.

So he came and asked me, (he said, in Japan?) He wanted me to go over there and do some concerts, and make a couple of albums. So I said fine. He was a very nice man. He'd been a jazz fan for years. He was all enthused with American jazz.

So he went back to Japan and told Koyama that I was interested. And finally he came over with his own photographer and the whole thing. Sometime when you come I'll show you the pictures they took. Really the pictures they took (in this magazine... ?). So that way we made (a connection?) and we went to Japan.
